subject: Discovery: inference bottleneck map & agreed next steps
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Amy Lin <amy@fintechco.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 16:18:00 -0700
Subject: Inference bottleneck mapping & next steps

Hi Amy — thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap from our side and the concrete next steps so we have shared alignment.

Key pain points you mentioned:
- Streamed responses feel jumpy at scale; users see long pauses before tokens arrive when concurrency spikes.
- Occasional 5xxs during big batch imports that coincide with nightly jobs.
- Cost is a constraint — need visibility into per-request token economics before committing to reserved capacity.

What you told us about current stack:
- Models served on Triton behind a gateway; internal KV cache for recent prefixes; some experimental sharding.
- Frontend uses a streaming client built on Server-Sent Events (SSE).
- Typical session length ~220 tokens; peak concurrent streams ~180; typical steady concurrency ~40.

Success criteria (agreed):
- p95 end-to-end latency for first streaming token <= 350ms under steady load (40 concurrent).
- Maintain max graceful degradation under burst to 200 concurrent streams — no more than 2% error rate.
- Cost target: keep per-1000-token effective compute below current baseline by >= 15% (measured over a 7-day window).

Immediate next steps (action owners):
1) Redwood: send a short bottleneck checklist and sample traces request (Hannah) — target: today EOD.
2) FintechCo: provide a recent netstat/trace and 24h token distribution (Amy / Sanjay) — target: Wed 4/7.
3) Schedule a tech deep-dive with Aditya to run through streaming UX optimizations and batching knobs — propose Thu 4/8 10am PT (Aditya/Hannah).

Attachments: I’m attaching a two-page checklist that will help us scope the deep-dive.

If anything above is inaccurate, flag and I’ll update. Otherwise we’ll treat this as the working plan and I’ll send calendar invites.

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Inference bottleneck mapping & next steps

Thanks Hannah — this is a helpful summary. A few clarifications and added detail from our infra side:

Clarifications:
- Steady-state p95 target should be interpreted as time-to-first-token for streaming use cases; we measured ~420ms on average today under steady load, spikes up to ~900ms during bursts.
- Peak concurrency often hits 220 in load tests; production peak is usually ~180 as I said, but occasional background work (exports) pushes it.

Current constraints and hints:
- We do autoscale Triton instances but scaling lag is ~60-90s which causes the transient p95 spikes.
- Network team sees occasional retransmits between frontend cluster and model hosts — attaching a short netstat sample.
- We do token caching at the application layer for repeated system prompts, but KV cache hit-rate is variable (20-40%).

We can provide: netstat dump (attached), 24h token histogram, and a short recording of the streaming UX (SSE).

One ask for Redwood before the deep-dive: can you outline the specific observability signals you’ll need so we can pull them from our stack? (traces, kernel tcp stats, Triton counters, gpu_utilization per instance, etc.)

Thanks — Amy
Amy Lin
Head of Product, FintechCo

Thanks Amy — good context. I pulled a short technical checklist together and annotated the key observability signals we’ll want to look at during the deep-dive. See inline below and attached PDF.

Short checklist (what we’ll probe in the session):
- Time-to-first-token path analysis: measure client-to-gateway, gateway-to-model, model decode time, and token emission cadence.
- KV cache effectiveness: sample hit/miss over 24h, distribution by prompt type.
- Batching behavior: current batch size distribution for requests and whether there’s batching on the gateway vs Triton.
- GPU scheduling stalls: look for long queue times or context-switch spikes.
- Network retransmits and RTOs: netstat + tcpdump around 95th percentile windows.
- Autoscaling lag: histogram of scale events and the corresponding p95 change.

Observability signals to gather (please export if possible):
- Triton request latency breakdown (request queue, infer, send).
- GPU utilization and per-GPU queue length.
- Application-level SSE emit timestamps (server-side token send times).
- Kernel-level TCP retransmit counters, RTT distributions.

Proposed tech deep-dive agenda (60 minutes):
- 10m: goal recap and success criteria alignment
- 20m: review traces and netstat sample live
- 15m: experiment plan — batching/kv-cache tuning + fallback strategies
- 10m: rollback/safety and instrumentation needs
- 5m: confirm next deliverables and owners

I’ve tentatively booked Thu 8 Apr 10:00am PT — sending the invite to all. If that time doesn’t work for you, suggest two alternatives.

Attachments: inference-bottleneck-checklist.pdf (annotated), sample-netstat-trace.txt

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
Senior Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
